title: return_expr_references_var treats every Call as scan-var-dependent, blocking IndexSeek for literal-arg calls (e.g. date("...") from $param substitution)
description:
Found in review of PR #154 (temporal $param support). property_value_to_return_expr
rewrites a temporal-valued param into a call to its own constructor, e.g.
date("2020-06-15") -- a ReturnExpr::Call with only literal args, no free
variables.

But return_expr_references_var (marsdb-query/src/planner.rs:454) conservatively
treats ANY ReturnExpr::Call as "might reference the scan var", defaulting to
"don't promote" for IndexSeek eligibility. So a query like:

  MATCH (m:Movie) WHERE m.released = $d

or the {released: row.date} shape inside a param-bound relationship-creation
statement, silently falls back to a full label scan per row instead of an
IndexSeek -- the exact perf trap this PR series (group commit + parameterized
loading) has been fighting, one dataset-with-dated-indexed-property away.

Fix: teach return_expr_references_var that a Call whose args are all
provably variable-free (recursively, via the same function) references
nothing either -- makes these row-independent and IndexSeekValue::Fixed-eligible,
without needing the larger Literal-widening change (adding a Literal::Date
variant) that's out of scope for the temporal-param work itself.

Verify with a real EXPLAIN-based test: MATCH (n:Label) WHERE n.indexedProp = $d
(with $d bound as a Date param) should show IndexSeek in the plan, not
NodeByLabelScan + Filter.

title: Phase 7: TCK runner fixture support (~43 unsup)
description:
MarsDB can run these queries but TCK runner can't parse expected-output fixtures. Fix runner:
- Named-path fixed-length output format (11) — path string representation
- Float literal very-long forms `.1e+308` (6) — parser doesn't accept
- Param-based list/map dynamic access `list[$p]` (10) — runner step parser doesn't handle
- `RETURN *` (1) — runner step parser
- Path variable forwarding (2)
- `UNWIND $param` (2) — list-valued parameter
- `null IN [...]` (1)
- Distinct-type ordering output (4)
- `keys($map)` (1)
- Other small (6)

Acceptance: +43 scenarios pass. All `RunnerUnsupported` drops to 0.

title: Phase 2: aggregate nested in expression (~25 scenarios)
description:
Allow aggregates inside wrapping arithmetic/function expressions. Real Cypher accepts `RETURN count(x) + 1`, `RETURN avg(a.age) * 2`, `RETURN max(a.age) + min(a.age)`. Currently MarsDB rejects "aggregate function must be a return item's entire expression".

Fix executor: compute aggregate first over group, then apply outer arithmetic using the grouped-then-aggregated values.

Acceptance: +25 scenarios pass. Return6, With6, ReturnOrderBy2, List12, Delete5 related tests green.

title: Phase 4: pattern comprehension (~11 scenarios)
description:
New expression syntax: `[ pattern | projection ]` where pattern is a graph pattern like `(n)-->()`. Correlated against outer scope, projects one row per match into a list.

Example: `RETURN [p = (n)-->() | p] AS list` for each `n` matched earlier.

Acceptance: +11 scenarios pass. Pattern2.feature all green.

title: VarExpand edge-isomorphism doesn't exclude a var-length hop's own edges from later hops
description:
LogicalPlan::VarExpand's exclude_edge_vars only seeds a variable-length hop's BFS with edges bound by EARLIER fixed hops of the same pattern -- the reverse direction (a variable-length hop's own internally-traversed edges being excluded by a LATER hop in the same pattern) isn't tracked at all. This causes a real double-count bug for patterns mixing a variable-length hop with another hop that reuses a relationship variable.

Found via TCK's Match4 [7]: `MATCH ()-[r:EDGE]-() MATCH p = (n)-[*0..1]-()-[r]-()-[*0..1]-(m) RETURN count(p) AS c` expects 32, got 52 -- confirmed via a full TCK run after briefly lifting parse_helpers.rs's validate_named_path_pattern restriction (which exists specifically to keep this gap unreachable for named-path capture). Reverted that lift (see commit 03b7fa7) rather than shipping the wrong result.

Also blocks TCK's Match6 [14]/[17] and Match7 [19] (named-path capture mixing a variable-length hop with another hop) -- those 3 scenarios don't happen to trigger the double-count themselves, but validate_named_path_pattern can't tell the difference between a pattern that would and one that wouldn't, so all mixing stays rejected together.

Real fix needs VarExpand's own BFS to also track its own traversed edges going forward into later hops' exclude_edge_vars (not just seed from earlier ones) -- likely means a per-row/per-candidate edge set needs to survive past the VarExpand stage into whatever hop comes next, not just get folded into an isomorphism check that only happens today for the *next hop's own* exclude_edge_vars, seeded once at plan-build time (planner.rs's prior_rel_vars), not per-row.

title: Phase 3: var-length path features (~34 scenarios)
description:
Two related features:
1. Bind variable to var-length rel `[r:TYPE*1..3]` — currently rejected as "binding a variable name to a variable-length relationship isn't supported". Should collect the list of relationships.
2. Named-path capture over var-length `p = (a)-[*]->(b)` — currently rejected as "named-path capture over a variable-length relationship pattern isn't supported". Should construct path value with nodes+rels in order.

Acceptance: +34 scenarios pass. Match4, Match6, Match7, Match9, Path2, Path3, Quantifier related tests green.

title: Wrong results for undirected multi-hop patterns with repeated end node
description:
TCK Match6[12] "Matching path with multiple bidirectional relationships" and Match5[27] "Handling mixed relationship patterns and directions 2" return wrong row counts (not errors) -- e.g. `MATCH p=(n)<-->(k)<-->(n) RETURN p` expects 4 rows, gets 2.

Not a regression from the ANTLR migration: pest's own TCK baseline (CYPHER_COVERAGE.md) shows wrong=0 for clauses/match -- pest's grammar apparently couldn't parse this `<-->`-shaped undirected-pattern-with-repeated-node shape at all (counted as reject). ANTLR's grammar parses it fine, newly exposing a latent executor.rs bug in path enumeration / edge-isomorphism handling for undirected multi-hop patterns where the end node repeats an earlier one.

Root cause not yet investigated -- likely in build_match_plan's Expand/edge-isomorphism logic (executor.rs) for the RelDirection::Either case combined with the "bound-node repetition" handling.
notes:
Partially fixed. Root cause found: build_relationship_pattern (antlr_visitor.rs) resolved a relationship pattern with BOTH arrowheads present (`<-[...]->`) as RelDirection::Left instead of RelDirection::Either (an `if LT ... else if GT ...` chain checked LT first, silently ignoring a simultaneously-present GT). Fixed to match on (LT present, GT present) properly: both-or-neither -> Either.

This fixed Match6[12] (now passes) and Create2[20]/Merge5-adjacent CREATE-with-both-arrows cases (now correctly hit the existing "CREATE/MERGE requires a directed relationship" check instead of silently succeeding with the wrong direction).

Still open: Match5[27] "Handling mixed relationship patterns and directions 2" -- still wrong result (expected 16 rows, got 0). Different shape: `<-[:LIKES*3]->` (undirected + variable-length hop combined). Likely a separate executor bug in variable-length traversal not correctly handling RelDirection::Either together with hop_range. Not yet investigated.

title: Phase C: aggregate composition, pattern comprehension, param widening
description: RETURN 1 + count(x) (Return6/With6, ~14 reject) -- generalize per-group evaluator beyond detect-and-reject. Pattern comprehension [(n)-->()|expr] (Pattern2, 11 reject). List/node/rel-valued query parameters (~20 unsup, needs PropertyValue/Value param-path widening in marsdb/marsdb-graph).

title: Named-path capture over a variable-length hop (MATCH p = (a)-[*..N]->(b))
description:
TCK: Quantifier1/2/3/4's [8]/[9] (8 reject) + ReturnOrderBy2 [12] (1 reject) -- all rejected with "named-path capture over a variable-length relationship pattern isn't supported yet". Also would fix Pattern2 [9] (pattern comprehension's own variable-length path capture, same underlying gap).

Root cause: assemble_path/name_pattern_for_path (executor.rs) walk pattern.hops expecting one (rel,node) token per hop with a single bound node/edge id each -- doesn't generalize to a variable-length hop, which represents a variable number of intermediate nodes/edges. expand_variable_row's BFS only tracks (final NodeId, used-edges HashSet) per candidate, not the ordered intermediate path.

Real fix needs the full ordered path (ordered Vec<EdgeId> alongside the existing HashSet, or equivalent) threaded through: VarExpandSpec/expand_variable_row (to build+bind the path), LogicalPlan::VarExpand (a new path_var field), and build_match_plan (to know when to set it -- currently doesn't receive path_var at all, that's handled by execute_match's own post-processing today). validate_named_path_pattern currently rejects this outright; needs relaxing for the single-hop, hop_range-present case specifically (leave multi-hop mixed fixed+variable path capture rejected, not tested by TCK).

Deliberately deferred this session (mars-858) -- contained but genuinely bigger than the other Phase D-adjacent fixes, touches the planner/IR, not just executor.rs.
